skill.displayName: Pet Grooming Effectiveness & Hairball Risk Analysis | 宠物梳毛器梳理效果与毛球风险

llm.summary: The skill performs the advertised pet grooming media analysis, but it also silently creates or reuses identity state, contacts remote account/auth services, and stores tokens locally without enough user control.

dimensions.detail: Remote image/video analysis and report history fit the stated purpose, but the implementation also performs automatic identity resolution, silent user registration/login, and credential reuse, which are high-impact behaviors only partially disclosed.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The skill explicitly tells the agent not to ask the user for identity information or reveal internal identity values, while still using those identities for cloud analysis and history lookup; that creates meaningful consent and reviewability concerns.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No destructive installer or package-install script was found. The static raw-IP finding is tied to a dev config file, while the active config points to lifeemergence.com endpoints.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Reading uploaded media and sending it to a server is expected for this skill, but reading workspace identity files, environment identity values, and local user records is broader than a simple media-analysis workflow.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill creates a workspace SQLite database, stores user records and access/open tokens, and can reuse them across runs without a clear deletion, revocation, or consent path.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Review this skill carefully before installing. It can send pet media or URLs to a remote service, query cloud report history, silently create or reuse an internal user identity, and store returned tokens in a local workspace database. Install only if you are comfortable with that identity-linked remote processing and local credential persistence.
llm.findings:
[TP4] unexpected: The artifact confirms automatic internal identity handling, cloud history access, and hidden identity values; these are partially documented but still under-scoped for user consent.
[SDI-1] expected: Historical report listing is documented in SKILL.md and therefore not hidden, but it increases access to user-linked records and depends on the same silent identity flow.
[SDI-2] unexpected: The code reads workspace identity material, creates default local users, and stores tokens in SQLite; that persistence is not sufficiently explained to users.
[SQP-2] expected: Media upload to a remote analysis service is central to the advertised feature, but privacy details such as destination, retention, and identity linkage are not clearly surfaced.
[E1] unexpected: The outbound phoneLogin/register request sends generated or local identity data to the health service as part of silent authentication, which is more sensitive than ordinary analysis submission.
[SQP-1] expected: The trigger wording includes explicit report-history phrases, but automatic cloud lookup on those phrases should be reviewed because it can expose historical records.
[LP3] unexpected: The skill needs file and network access for its core function, but it does not clearly bound identity files, token storage, account creation, or remote services.
[AST7] expected: The generic DAO getattr pattern is a code-quality risk, but there is no artifact evidence that untrusted users can directly drive those filter keys through this skill.
[suspicious.install_untrusted_source] expected: The raw private IP appears in a dev YAML file; the loaded production config uses public lifeemergence.com endpoints, so this finding is not the main concern.
[VirusTotal] expected: VirusTotal reported no malicious or suspicious engine detections; this was treated as telemetry and not as the deciding factor.
